newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turks in blackout protest to illuminate scandal.
newsitem.headline: Turks in blackout protest to illuminate scandal.

text.p: Turks began a campaign on Saturday to plunge their houses into darkness to throw some light on a scandal involving government links with the criminal underworld.

Starting a month-long protest, which was broadcast live on television, leading businessman Sakip Sabanci blacked out the well-known twin towers of his Sabanci Center in Istanbul's central Levent district.
Journalist Fatih Altayli, one of the campaigners, said a few other districts in Istanbul were plunged completely into darkness and some partially blacked out.

Several houses in the leftist Cankaya district of Ankara also turned their lights out at 1900 GMT and some people banged on pans and other household utensils to mark the first night of a month-long protest campaign, entitled "A minute's darkness for eternal light".
The response in other cities was unclear.
"I find this a very positive thing and I give it my full support," former social democrat culture minister Ercan Karakas told NTV television.

The protest aims to press the government to resolve the scandal stemming from a crash on November 3 when a top policeman and a wanted gangster died in the same car. A government MP in the same car was injured.
An investigation into state ties to the underworld has produced no results, but the media has repeated claims that the state is infiltrated by crime gangs.
The protest is officially organised by people describing themselves as "ordinary citizens", but many leftist parties, journalists and businessmen have pledged their support.
